title: Surveying
description: Digitized question bank covering Surveying Chapter 4 topics: levelling, bearings, contouring, curves, tacheometry, chain/compass/plane-table/theodolite surveying, traversing, and numericals.

questions.text: If the Reduced Level of Bench Mark is 105m, the back sight is 1.235m and the foresight is 1.920m, then what is the Reduced Level of forward station?
For a distance of 1800m, what will be the corrections for curvature and refraction?
In a levelling work, sum of back sight and fore sight have been found to be 3.085m and 5.645m respectively. If the reduced level of starting station is 100.00m, the RL of last station is
The latitude of a 50m line having bearing S 40°W is
questions.expl: Latitude = -L cosθ = -50 cos40° = -38.3m (southerly, hence negative).

questions.text: If the whole circle bearing is 211°54', then the quadrantal bearing is:
questions.expl: WCB in 180-270° range (SW quadrant): RB = WCB-180 = 31°54', so S31°54'W.

questions.text: If the tangent length for a simple curve is 12m and the chainage of the point of intersection is 360m, then the chainage of the starting point of the curve is:
questions.expl: Chainage of start of curve = PI chainage - tangent length = 360-12 = 348m.

questions.text: A back sight reading on B.M. = 100m was 3.50m. The inverted staff reading to the bottom of a girder was 1.50m. The R.L. of the bottom of girder is
questions.expl: HI = 100+3.50 = 103.50m; for inverted staff, RL = HI + reading = 103.50+1.50 = 105.0m.

questions.text: A 30m metric chain is found to be 10cm too short throughout a measurement. If the distance measured is recorded as 300m, what is the actual distance?
The ratio of the sum of the exterior angles to sum of interior angles of a closed octagonal traverse will be
questions.expl: Standard exam answer for this octagon traverse angle-sum ratio question is 17/15.

questions.text: The bearing of the sun at local noon, observed with a prismatic compass, was 184°30'. If the bearing of a line, measured with the compass, was found to be 15°30', then what would be the true bearing of the line?
options: cannot be estimated with given data
questions.expl: Sun's true bearing at noon is 180°, so instrument error = +4°30'; True bearing of line = 15°30' - 4°30' = 11°00'.

questions.text: A man from the top of a 100m high tower sees a car moving towards the tower at an angle of depression of 30°. After sometime, the angle of depression becomes 60°. What would be the distance travelled by the car during this time?

To determine the tacheometric constants K and C, distances of 30m and 60m were measured at stations P and Q. Stadia readings at P: 1.130, 1.280, 1.430; at Q: 1.025, 1.325, 1.620. What are the values of K and C?
questions.expl: Intercept at P=0.300, at Q=0.595. Solving 0.300K+C=30 and 0.595K+C=60 gives K=101.695, C=-0.51.

questions.text: The three consecutive readings taken with a level instrument are 1.325m, 0.985m, and 2.546m. If the instrument was shifted after the first reading, then what would be the rise or fall of the last point?
If the R.L. of a B.M. is 100.00m, the back-sight is 1.215m and the foresight is 1.870m, the R.L. of the forward station is
If the true bearing of a line AB is 269°30', then the azimuth of the line AB is
questions.expl: Azimuth measured from North equals the true bearing here: 269°30'.

questions.text: If the intercept on a vertical staff is observed as 0.75m from a tacheometer, the horizontal distance between tacheometer and staff station is
questions.expl: Distance = K×s = 100×0.75 = 75m (standard K=100, C=0).

questions.text: If the coordinates of A are 100N and 200E and those of C are 100S and 200E, then the length AC is
questions.expl: ΔLatitude=200 (100N to 100S), ΔDeparture=0; length AC = 200.00.

questions.text: The fore bearings of the lines AB, BC, CD and DE are 45°30', 120°15', 200°30' and 280°45' respectively. ∠B and ∠C will be
The magnetic bearing of a line is S25°30'E. If the magnetic declination is 5°30' West, the true bearing of the line is:
questions.expl: True bearing = Magnetic bearing − westerly declination = S25°30'E − 5°30' = S20°00'E.

questions.text: The observed reading on a staff held at point A is 3.55 m, if the staff is found to be 0.10 m off the vertical through its bottom, the correct staff reading on point A is:
If the length of image is 0.030 m and the length of the actual staff covered is 0.90 m, then the magnifying power of telescope is:
questions.expl: Magnifying power = staff length / image length = 0.90/0.030 = 30.

questions.text: By using a tacheometer with a horizontal line of sight, the three hair readings are recorded as 2.100, 1.852 and 1.534 m. If the multiplying constant is 100 and additive constant is zero, then the distance between the instrument and stadia rod station is:
questions.expl: Stadia intercept = 2.100−1.534 = 0.566m; Distance = 100×0.566 = 56.60m.

questions.text: The combined correction for curvature and refraction for a point located at 2 km distance is:
Find out the deviation angle where a vertical summit curve is formed at the intersection of two gradients, +3.0% and −5.0%.
The length of a chain line measured along a slope is 300.50 m. If the slope of the ground is 5°, the horizontal distance is ___.
questions.expl: Horizontal distance = L cosθ = 300.50 × cos5° = 299.36m.

questions.text: A level is set up at O on a line AB 20 m from A and 1200 m from B. The BS on A is 0.532 m and the FS on B is 3.425 m. The combined correction to be applied for 20 m distance is:
questions.expl: The correction for the very short 20m distance is negligible, effectively 0m.

questions.text: The readings on staff which is held vertically 60 m from a tacheometer are 1.460 and 2.055. The line of sight is horizontal. If the focal length of objective is 20 cm and the distance from objective lens to the vertical axis is 13 cm, the additive constant is:
questions.expl: Additive constant C = f + d = 0.20 + 0.13 = 0.33m.

questions.text: The length of a line measured with a 30 m chain is 800.64 m. Afterwards it is found that the chain is 0.05 m too long. The true length of the line is:
The whole circle bearing of a line measured is 135°. The reduced bearing of line is:
questions.expl: WCB 135° lies in the SE quadrant (90°-180°): RB = 180-135 = S45°E.

questions.text: What is the magnetic declination if the sum of the magnetic bearing at a place known in southern hemisphere is 167°?
questions.expl: Based on the standard calculation for this problem type, the declination is 13° W.

questions.text: In setting up of plane table at a point P, the corresponding point on the plan was not accurately centered above the point P. If the displacement of P was 20 cm in a direction at right angles to the ray, how much on the plan would be the consequent displacement of a point from its true position, if scale is 1 cm = 100 m?
questions.expl: Plan displacement = 20cm × (1/10000) = 0.002cm = 0.02mm.

questions.text: A 20 m length chain got out of the correct line by a perpendicular distance of 1 m, then the associated error in meters is:
questions.expl: Error = (perpendicular distance)² / (2 × chain length) = 1² / (2×20) = 1/40.

questions.text: If a curve is designated as a 3° curve on a 40 m arc, the radius of the curve is:
The magnetic bearing of a line is 44°35'. If the magnetic declination is 4°14' East, the true bearing is:
questions.expl: True bearing = Magnetic + easterly declination = 44°35' + 4°14' = 48°49'.

questions.text: If the radius of a curve is 360 m and length of arch is 24 m, then the degree of designation of curve is:
If the fore bearing of a line is observed to AB 12°24', the back bearing of the line AB should be?
questions.expl: Back bearing = Fore bearing + 180° = 12°24' + 180° = 192°24'.

questions.text: The distance between two pegs P and Q is chained. Before reaching peg Q, the back man has used 10 chains and also, he has counted 15 links from last arrow to peg Q. If the length of chain is 20 m and length of one link is 0.2 m, the total distance between pegs P and Q is:
The fore bearing of a line measured at 60°, the back bearing of the same line is:
questions.expl: Back bearing = Fore bearing + 180° = 60° + 180° = 240°.

questions.text: All the dimensions of the embankment were measured with 20m chain and the volume was calculated as 368.85 cubic meter. It was then found that the chain was 10cm too long. Find the true volume of embankment?
A 40 m chain was tested before a survey and found to have a length of 39.95 m. If the length of line measured with this chain was 384.56m, then find the true length of the line.
The whole circle bearings of a traverse are recorded as: AB=70°30', BC=120°, CD=223°30', DA=320°47'. Convert these to reduced bearings for BC and CD.
questions.expl: Converting each WCB to its quadrant gives reduced bearings of S59°15'E for BC and N53°30'W for CD.

questions.text: What will be the bearing of a line AB, if its magnetic bearing is S28°30'E and the declination is 7°30' west?
questions.expl: WCB of magnetic bearing=151°30'; True WCB=151°30'-7°30'=144°00', which converts to S36°00'E.

questions.text: A 20 m steel tape was standardized at a temperature of 30°C under a pull of 5 kg. The tape was used in catenary to fix a distance of 20 m between two points at 40°C under a pull of 10 Kg. To arrive at the total correction (subtractive), the correction for Temperature is calculated using which of the following formulas?
questions.expl: The standard temperature correction formula is Ct = a(Tm − T0)L.

questions.text: The distance between two points measured with a 30 m chain was 300 m. It was afterwards found that the chain was 3 cm too long. What will be the true distance of the line between the points (in m)?
A level was set up at a point A and distance to the staff station B was 100 m. The net combined correction due to curvature and refraction as applied to the staff reading is
questions.expl: C = 0.0673×(0.1)² = 0.000673m, applied as a subtractive (negative) correction to the staff reading.

questions.text: If three consecutive ordinates are taken at 2 m intervals from a traverse line and measured as 1.8 m, 2.5 m and 2.0 m, then the area between the traverse line, the first and last ordinates and the boundary, by trapezoidal rule, is
If the area calculated from the plan plotted with measurements by an erroneous chain, then the accurate area of the plan is:
options: Measured area × (Length of chain used/Nominal length of chain)
Measured area × (Nominal length of chain/Length of chain used)
Measured area × (Length of chain used/Nominal length of chain)²
Measured area × (Nominal length of chain/Length of chain used)²
questions.expl: True area = Measured area × (L used/L nominal)².

questions.text: A hill was photographed at a constant flying height of 4000 m above mean sea level (MSL). If the axis of the camera was truly vertical and its optical (focal) length was 12.5 cm and the height of the hill was 700 m, then the scale of the photograph will be:
The Whole Circle Bearing of line AB is 50° and of line BC is 120°. The deflection angle at B from AB to BC is:
questions.expl: Deflection angle = 120° − 50° = 70°.

questions.text: A bubble tube with divisions of 2 mm and a radius of 10 m has the sensitivity of about:
A backsight (B.S.) is taken on station 'A' and found to be = 3.0 m. A foresight on station 'B' = 2.5 m w.r.t. station A. The R.L. of station B is 100.00, then what is the R.L. of station A?
If the focal length of the object glass is 25 cm and the distance from object glass to the trunnion axis is 15 cm, the additive constant is
questions.expl: Additive constant = f + d = 0.25 + 0.15 = 0.4m.

questions.text: If the magnetic bearing of the line is S32°E and the magnetic declination is 8°16', then the true bearing of the line will be
questions.expl: WCB of magnetic bearing = 148°; True WCB = 148°+8°16' = 156°16', converting to S23°44'E.

questions.text: If the reduced bearing of the line is N58°24'W, then the whole circle bearing of the line will be

In leveling between two points A & B on opposite banks of a river, staff readings on A & B were 2.243 & 3.31 (level near A), then 1.889 & 3.041 (level near B). What is the true level difference between A and B?
questions.expl: True difference = average of (3.31−2.243) and (3.041−1.889) = average of 1.067 and 1.152 = 1.10m.

questions.text: 6h 42m 34s in degrees minutes seconds will be

A temporary bench mark has been established at the soffit of a chejja on a window opening, and its known elevation is 102.405 m above mean sea level. The backsight used to establish the height of the instrument is by an inverted staff reading of 1.80 m. A foresight reading with the same staff, held normally, is 1.215 m on a recently constructed plinth. The elevation of the plinth is
The rate of rainfall for successive 30 min periods of a 3-hour storm are: 1.6, 3.6, 5.0, 2.8, 2.2 and 1.0 cm/hour. The corresponding surface runoff is estimated to be 3.2 cm. Then, the φ index is
questions.expl: By trial, φ=1.8cm/h gives excess rainfall of 3.2cm, matching the given runoff.

questions.text: The combined correction for curvature and refraction for a distance of 1400 m is
The correction for sag is
questions.expl: Sag causes the tape to read long, so the correction is always subtractive.

questions.text: In surveying, working from whole to part leads to:
questions.expl: Working from whole to part helps minimize the accumulation of errors.

questions.text: Which of the following angles has spherical excess?
questions.expl: An angle greater than 180° (like 225°) reflects spherical excess in this context (sum exceeding plane triangle expectations).

questions.text: Theory of probability can be applied to
options: None of the above is correct
questions.expl: The theory of probability applies to accidental (random) errors.

questions.text: Closed contours with lower value inwards, represent a
questions.expl: Lower values inward indicate a depression; higher values inward indicate a hill.

questions.text: The method of interpolation of contours which is extremely rough and is used for small scale work is:
questions.expl: The graphical method is a rough, quick method suitable for small scale work.

questions.text: In the case of hilly terrain, which method is used to locate the contours?
questions.expl: Cross-section method is commonly used for contouring hilly terrain.

questions.text: A plane surface on a contour map is indicated by
options: series of straight parallel and equal spaced contours
questions.expl: A uniform plane slope is shown by straight, parallel, equally spaced contours.

questions.text: Which of the following methods of contouring is most suitable for a hilly terrain?
questions.expl: The tacheometric method is efficient for locating contours in hilly terrain.

questions.text: Select the correct statement
options: contour interval on any map is kept constant
direct method of contouring is cheaper than indirect method
inter-visibility of points on a contour map cannot be ascertained
slope of a hill cannot be determined with the help of contours
questions.expl: Contour interval is kept uniform/constant throughout a given map.

questions.text: The line joining the points having the same elevation above the datum surface, is called a:
questions.expl: This is the definition of a contour line.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not possible to obtain through contour plan?
questions.expl: Determining inter-visibility (or its absence) between stations is not a standard direct use of a contour plan in this context.

questions.text: The line which is the intersection of a level surface with the ground is called:
questions.expl: This defines a contour line.

questions.text: In which of the following cases, the two contour lines intersect each other?
questions.expl: Contour lines only intersect in the special case of an overhanging vertical cliff.

questions.text: Which one of the following scales is used to plot contour map?
questions.expl: A contour map is plotted using the horizontal scale of the map.

questions.text: The angle made by a contour line passing through a point with a line of maximum slope at that point is:
questions.expl: A line of maximum slope is always perpendicular (90°) to the contour line.

questions.text: Which one of the following contour methods is employed in route surveys for roads?
questions.expl: Cross-section method is commonly used for contouring in route surveys.

questions.text: Two contour lines of same elevation:
options: Cannot unite and continue as one line.
Cannot unite and but continue as one line.
Can unite and but not continue as one line.
Can unite and continue as one line.
questions.expl: Contours of the same elevation can unite (e.g. at a vertical cliff) and continue as one line.

questions.text: Difference in elevation between two successive contour lines is called:
questions.expl: This defines the contour interval.

questions.text: A contour map which has higher elevations inside is the example of:
questions.expl: Higher elevations inside closed contours indicate a hillock/hill.

questions.text: Which of the following method is used for locating points on the ground by distance measurement and finding their elevations using a level?
questions.expl: Contouring locates points and their elevations using grid/section methods combined with levelling.

questions.text: What is the horizontal distance between successive contours called?
questions.expl: This defines the horizontal equivalent.

questions.text: Select the correct statement:
options: Closed contours with higher values inwards represent a depression.
The contour lines crossing a valley have higher values on the convex side.
Profile leveling is done for determining the contour.
The horizontal and vertical scales in a longitudinal section are generally equal.
questions.expl: Contour lines crossing a valley bend upstream, with higher values on the convex side.

questions.text: Curves of equal depth are called:
questions.expl: Curves of equal depth (underwater) are called isobaths.

questions.text: The characteristics of contours are:
options: Closer drawn contours show steep slopes
questions.expl: All of these are standard characteristics of contour lines.

questions.text: Contour interval is
options: inversely proportional to the scale of the map
directly proportional to the scale of the map
larger if the time available is more
questions.expl: Contour interval is generally inversely proportional to the map scale.

questions.text: Select the correct statement.
options: A contour is not necessarily a closed curve.
A contour represents a ridge line if the concave side of lower value contour lies towards the higher value contour.
Two contours of different elevations do not cross each other except in case of an overhanging cliff.
All of the above statements are correct.
questions.expl: All the given statements about contours are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following methods estimates best the area of an irregular and curved boundary?
questions.expl: Simpson's rule fits a parabolic curve, best suited for curved irregular boundaries.

questions.text: The great disadvantage of tacheometry is that it needs to elaborate calculations to find out the
options: horizontal distances and elevations of points
questions.expl: Tacheometric reduction requires elaborate calculations for both horizontal distance and elevation.

questions.text: For a tacheometer the additive and multiplying constants are respectively
questions.expl: Standard tacheometer constants: additive constant = 0, multiplying constant = 100.

questions.text: The great disadvantage of tacheometry is that it needs to elaborate calculations to find out the
options: horizontal distances and elevations of points
questions.expl: Tacheometric reduction requires elaborate calculation of both horizontal distance and elevation.

questions.text: In a Tacheometry survey of distance formula, the additive constant is expressed as:
options: (Focal length of objective lens) + (Distance from objective lens to vertical axis)
(Focal length of objective lens) − (Distance from objective lens to vertical axis)
(Distance from objective lens to vertical axis) / (Focal length of objective lens)
(Focal length of objective lens) / (Distance from objective lens to vertical axis)
questions.expl: Additive constant C = f + d (focal length + distance from objective to vertical axis).

questions.text: Which one of the following expressions gives horizontal distance for horizontal line of sight and vertical circle reading is zero? (Where K and S are constants)
questions.expl: For horizontal sight, horizontal distance D = Ks + C.

questions.text: The principle involved in movable hair tacheometry is:
options: Trigonometry is used for measurement of distance.
By moving the stadia wires a constant intercept on the staff can be obtained.
Distance can be estimated by measuring two vertical angles.
Distance is proportional to the intercepts on a stadia rod.
questions.expl: In movable hair (Subtense) tacheometry, the stadia wires are moved to obtain a constant staff intercept.

questions.text: In a tacheometry, when line of sight is inclined with an angle of elevation and staff is held vertical, the horizontal distance is given as:
questions.expl: For an inclined sight to a vertical staff, D = Ks cos²θ + C cosθ.

questions.text: Distance measured by instruments using radio or light waves, geodimeters, tachometry come under which measurement method?
questions.expl: These are all indirect distance measurement methods.

questions.text: Which of the given branches of surveying is used to measure horizontal and vertical distances without the use of chain and tape?
questions.expl: Telemetry (electronic distance measurement) measures distances without chain or tape.

questions.text: The correct sequence in which these surveys are conducted before the alignment of a track is finalised is:
questions.expl: Order: Reconnaissance, Traffic survey, Preliminary survey, Location survey.

questions.text: Which of the following closely represents the shape of the earth?
questions.expl: The earth closely approximates an oblate spheroid (flattened at poles).

questions.text: The working from whole to part is done in surveying in order to ensure that:
options: survey work is completed more quickly
errors and mistakes of one portion do not affect the remaining portion
questions.expl: Working from whole to part prevents accumulation/propagation of errors across the survey.

questions.text: Identify the CORRECT order of engineering surveys for highway alignment.
options: Map study, Reconnaissance survey, Preliminary survey and Final location and Detailed surveys
Reconnaissance survey, Final location and detailed surveys, Map study and Preliminary survey
Final location and detailed surveys, Map study, Reconnaissance survey, Preliminary survey
Preliminary survey, Final location and Detailed surveys, Map study and Reconnaissance survey
questions.expl: The correct sequence is: Map study, Reconnaissance survey, Preliminary survey, Final location and Detailed surveys.

questions.text: The earliest surveys were made in connection with:
questions.expl: The earliest surveys were connected with land surveys/land distribution.

questions.text: Which of the following surveying is commonly conducted for specifying national boundaries and land use patterns?
questions.expl: Geographical surveys deal with national boundaries and land use patterns.

questions.text: Classification of the archaeological survey is based on:
questions.expl: Archaeological survey classification is based on the object/purpose of the survey.

questions.text: Which of the following surveys is conducted for work requiring high precision?
questions.expl: Geodetic surveys are conducted with the highest degree of precision.

questions.text: Which one of the following surveys is used for economic importance for a country?
questions.expl: Geological surveys hold significant economic importance (mineral wealth, resources).

questions.text: Which one of the following surveys is NOT based upon the nature of the field survey?
questions.expl: Astronomical survey classification is based on the method/purpose, not the nature of the field survey.

questions.text: Location surveys are used for:
options: Setting out the work on the ground
Determining the feasibility of the area
questions.expl: Location surveys are used to set out (transfer) the final alignment on the ground.

questions.text: Which of the following surveys is done to produce plans of property boundaries for legal purposes?
questions.expl: Cadastral surveys establish property boundaries for legal purposes.

questions.text: The purpose of geological survey is:
questions.expl: Geological surveys are primarily conducted to explore mineral wealth.

questions.text: Engineering survey in which Centre line of the road is transferred on the ground in:
questions.expl: The centre line is transferred to the ground during the final location and detailed survey.

questions.text: The Cadastral survey is used for:
options: Determining natural features of a country
questions.expl: Cadastral survey is used to determine the boundaries of fields/properties.

questions.text: Which of the following is carried out to map places of military and strategic importance?
questions.expl: Purpose-based surveying includes military/strategic surveys.

questions.text: Which of the following surveys is undertaken to define and record the boundary of properties, legislative area and even countries?
questions.expl: Cadastral surveying is used to record property, legislative, and national boundaries.

questions.text: Which of the following is recommended when the area is large, undulating and crowded with many details?
questions.expl: Topographic surveying is recommended for large, undulating, detail-rich areas.

questions.text: Mine surveying is used for
questions.expl: Mine surveying is conducted for exploring mineral wealth.

questions.text: In a whole circle bearing system, S25°15'E corresponds to
If the declination is to the east, then the true bearing can be calculated from the observed magnetic bearing by the relation:
questions.expl: For easterly declination, True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination.

questions.text: The systematic departure of the declination from its mean value during a period of 24hrs is known as
questions.expl: Diurnal variation is the daily systematic change in declination.

questions.text: The permanent adjustment of both prismatic and surveyor's compass includes:
questions.expl: Permanent adjustment includes adjustment of the levels (bubble).

questions.text: The magnetic declination variation at a place due to magnetic storms is called as
questions.expl: Irregular variation is caused by unpredictable events like magnetic storms.

questions.text: Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to
options: incorrect levelling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
pressure of magnetic substances near the instrument
questions.expl: Local attraction is caused by magnetic substances near the compass station.

questions.text: If the fore bearing of a line is N 26°35'W, its back bearing will be:
questions.expl: Back bearing = Fore bearing ± 180°; N26°35'W becomes S26°35'E.

questions.text: In Sexagesimal system, one circumference is equal to ___.
questions.expl: In the sexagesimal system, a full circle is 360°.

questions.text: The direction of magnetic meridian at a place:
options: is always equal to true meridian
questions.expl: The magnetic meridian's direction changes with time due to declination variation.

questions.text: Which one of the following is CORRECT as per the requirements of magnetic needle?
options: Centre of gravity of needle should necessarily be below the pivot.
Needle should not necessarily be straight.
The ends of needle need not necessarily be in the same plane.
Needle should not necessarily be sensitive.
questions.expl: For stability, the needle's centre of gravity should be below the pivot point.

questions.text: Compass surveying is useful compared to chain surveying when:
options: Uneven terrain needs to be surveyed
A small area needs to be covered in great detail
Chain Survey tools are not available
A large area needs to be covered
questions.expl: Compass surveying is preferable for uneven/obstructed terrain where chaining is difficult.

questions.text: In surveyor's compass, the graduations are shown as
questions.expl: The surveyor's compass reads 0° at North/South and 90° at East/West.

questions.text: The directions of survey lines are fixed by angular measurements and not by forming a network of triangles. This statement is true for which type of surveying?
questions.expl: Compass surveying fixes directions using bearings (angular measurement) rather than triangulation.

questions.text: Which given statement is true:
options: The whole circle bearing of a line can be converted to quadrantal bearing by reducing it to an angle less than 90° which has the same numerical value of the trigonometric functions.
The whole circle bearing of a line can be converted to quadrantal bearing by increasing it to an angle greater than 90° which has the same numerical value of the trigonometric functions.
The whole circle bearing of a line can be converted to quadrantal bearing by increasing it to an angle less than 45° which has the same numerical value of the trigonometric functions.
The whole circle bearing of a line can be converted to quadrantal bearing by reducing it to an angle greater than 180° which has the same numerical value of the trigonometric functions.
questions.expl: WCB is converted to QB by reducing it to an equivalent angle less than 90°.

questions.text: For plotting a compass survey which of the following method is used and more accurate?
questions.expl: The rectangular coordinate method gives the most accurate plotting of a compass survey.

questions.text: Traversing with magnetic bearings method is suitable for ___.
options: Places where local attraction due to external magnetic field influences is present
Places where local attraction due to external magnetic field influences is absent
questions.expl: Magnetic bearing traversing is suitable only where local attraction is absent.

questions.text: In the compass surveying, the line joining places of the same dip are called
questions.expl: Isoclinic lines join places of equal dip.

questions.text: In the compass surveying, Isogonic lines are
options: the line joining in the places of the zero dip
The lines joining points of equal declination at time of observation.
The line joining in the place of the same dip
The line joining in the place of the zero declination
questions.expl: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination.

questions.text: Least count of prismatic compass and surveyor's compass is
questions.expl: The prismatic compass has a least count of 30 minutes, and the surveyor's compass has 15 minutes.

questions.text: If the true bearing of a line AB is 269°30', then the azimuth of the line AB is
questions.expl: Azimuth measured from North equals the true bearing here: 269°30'.

questions.text: Statement (I): Compass survey is still used by geologists to locate magnetic ores. Statement (II): Local attraction causes errors in compass survey due to terrestrial features – either natural or manmade.
options: Both I and II are true, and II correctly explains I
Both I and II are true, but II does not explain I
I is true, II is false
I is false, II is true
questions.expl: Both statements are independently true, though statement II does not directly explain statement I.

questions.text: Magnetic bearing of a line is the
options: horizontal angle which it makes with the magnetic meridian
vertical angle which it makes with the magnetic meridian
vertical angle which it makes with the magnetic meridian
questions.expl: Magnetic bearing is the horizontal angle a line makes with the magnetic meridian.

questions.text: The direction of a line relative to a given meridian is known as?
questions.expl: This defines the bearing of a line.

questions.text: The process of determining the plotted position of the station occupied by the plane table, by means of sights taken towards known points, is known as
questions.expl: This is the definition of the resection method.

questions.text: Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
questions.expl: Non-horizontality of the board is an instrumental error; others are manipulation/personal errors.

questions.text: In solving a three point problem, using trial and error method, the strength of fix is good under which one of the following situations?
options: The station occupied by the plane table lies within the circle passing through the three points
The station occupied by the plane table lies within the triangle formed by three points.
The station occupied by the plane table lies near the circle passing through the three points
questions.expl: The fix is good when the station lies near the circumscribing circle of the three points.

questions.text: The three-point problem in plane tabling involves
options: determining positions of the three points in the field
locating the stations occupied by the plane table in the sheet with positions of three points in the field
locating the positions of two points in the field with one fixed point
surveying any area with three points
questions.expl: The three-point problem locates the plane table station on the sheet using three known points.

questions.text: Which one of the following instruments is used in plane table surveying for the measurement of horizontal and vertical distance directly?
questions.expl: The telescopic alidade allows direct tacheometric measurement of distances.

questions.text: Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for:
questions.expl: Intersection method is well suited to hilly/rugged areas where direct measurement is difficult.

questions.text: The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously is known as:
questions.expl: Plane tabling allows simultaneous field observation and graphical plotting.

questions.text: The objective of two-point problem which is solved with the resection method is:
options: Given location of two points, locating the station occupied by the plane table
Locating the plane table station point
Locating two previous stations occupied by the plane table
questions.expl: The two-point problem locates the plane table station using two known points.

questions.text: A telescopic alidade provides:
questions.expl: A telescopic alidade provides an accurate line of sight for sighting distant/inclined objects.

questions.text: By which of the following plane table surveying methods, the two-point problem is solved?
questions.expl: The two-point problem is solved using the resection method.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not the adjustments of the plane table?
options: The surface of the board should be perfect plane.
The ruling of fiducial edge of the alidade should be straight.
The sight vanes of the alidade should be perpendicular to the base of the ruler.
The bubble on spirit level need not be at center.
questions.expl: The bubble should be at the centre for correct levelling; this statement is incorrect and hence not a valid adjustment requirement.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT the error due to manipulation and sighting in plane table survey?
questions.expl: Error of plotting is a drafting error, not a manipulation/sighting error.

questions.text: In solving three point problem by trial and error process, the fix strength is good when:
options: The angle subtended by the two lines obtained by joining the three points is very small
The station occupied by the plane table lies on the circle passing through the three points
The station occupied by the plane table lies near the circle passing through the three points
The station occupied by the plane table lies within the triangle formed by the three points
questions.expl: The fix is good when the station lies near the circle passing through the three points.

questions.text: ___ is the essential method of orienting a table.
questions.expl: Traversing is commonly used as the essential method of orienting a plane table in the field.

questions.text: The plane table can be used for
questions.expl: The plane table can be used for traversing, resection, and intersection.

questions.text: Which of the following is not the equipment for plane table survey?
questions.expl: Plumbing, spirit level, and compass are all standard plane table equipment.

questions.text: After fixing the plane table to the tripod, the main operations needed at each plane table station are: a. Levelling b. Orientation c. Centering. The correct sequence for this operation is
questions.expl: The correct sequence is Centering, Levelling, then Orientation.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The plane table surveying does not require office work
Detailed plotting is generally done by radiation
An inaccessible detail can be located by intersection
In three-point problem, the station is easily located when it falls on the great circle
questions.expl: This is incorrect: plane table surveying does still require some office work.

questions.text: The two-point problem as compared to the three-point problem is:
questions.expl: The two-point problem is generally more laborious than the three-point problem.

questions.text: The process of determining the plotted position of the station occupied by the plane table by means of sights taken towards points of known location is called:
questions.expl: This defines the resection method.

questions.text: One of the Lehmann's rules of plane tabling, is
options: when looking in the direction of each of the given points, the instrument station will be on the right side of one and left side of the other ray
when the instrument station is outside the circumscribing circle, its location is always on the opposite side of the ray to the most distant point as the intersection of its other two rays.
location of the instrument station is always distant from each of the three rays from the known points in proportion to their distances.
questions.expl: This is one of Lehmann's rules for the three-point problem.

questions.text: The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane table station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
questions.expl: The fix is bad (indeterminate) when the station lies on the circumscribing circle.

questions.text: Which of the following methods of plane table surveying is used to locate the position of an inaccessible point?
questions.expl: The intersection method is used to locate inaccessible points.

questions.text: When compared with Chain Surveying, Plane table is:
questions.expl: Plane table surveying is generally less accurate than chain surveying.

questions.text: The process of turning the telescope in a horizontal plane is known as
questions.expl: Rotating the telescope about the vertical axis is called swinging.

questions.text: In theodolite work, error in manipulation comes under
questions.expl: Errors in manipulation and sighting are classed as personal errors.

questions.text: Removal of parallax may be achieved by
options: refocusing the eyepiece and the objective
questions.expl: Parallax is removed by focusing both the eyepiece (for the cross-hairs) and the objective (for the image).

questions.text: The removal of parallax, in a theodolite, can be achieved by which one of the following processes?
questions.expl: Refocusing the objective brings the image onto the plane of the cross-hairs, removing parallax.

questions.text: Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking the mean of both the faces of theodolite?
options: Errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to the horizontal axis
questions.expl: Taking face-left and face-right observations eliminates collimation-type instrumental errors.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the correct one as per the reiteration method?
options: The angle is measured three times each using face left and face right observations.
The same angle is measured by face left and by face right observations.
The angle is measured, and the instrument turned to close the horizon.
The same angle is measured three times.
questions.expl: In the reiteration (direction) method, all angles are measured successively and the instrument is turned to close the horizon.

questions.text: Turning the telescope in a horizontal plane is called:
questions.expl: Rotating the telescope about the vertical axis is called swinging.

questions.text: The horizontal circle in a theodolite is graduated in:
options: The quadrantal system from 0 to 90° in the four quadrants
Similar to that of prismatic compass
The whole circle system from 0 to 360°
The semi-circle system from 0 to 180° in the right and left halves
questions.expl: Theodolite horizontal circles are graduated on the whole circle system, 0° to 360°.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not the errors due to natural cause in the theodolite?
options: Settlement of tripod due to soft soil
questions.expl: Slip is an instrumental/personal error, not a natural-cause error.

questions.text: Which one of the following operations is not done by the theodolite?
questions.expl: A theodolite measures both horizontal and vertical angles, not only horizontal ones.

questions.text: Transiting is the process of rotating the telescope about the horizontal axis through 180°, the telescope pointing in the opposite direction after transiting. The process is known as
questions.expl: This process (rotating about the horizontal axis) is also called plunging.

questions.text: In which of the following theodolites can the telescope be rotated in a vertical plane?
questions.expl: A vernier (transit) theodolite allows the telescope to rotate fully in the vertical plane.

questions.text: For a theodolite instrument certain Permanent adjustments are done from time to time. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT with respect to these adjustments?
options: The axis of the plate level must be perpendicular to the vertical axis
The line of collimation must be at right angles to the horizontal axis
The axis of telescope level must be parallel to the line of collimation
The Horizontal axis must be parallel to the vertical axis
questions.expl: This is incorrect: the horizontal axis must be perpendicular (not parallel) to the vertical axis.

questions.text: Two points are marked on the ground where the line of sight strikes before and after plunging the telescope and a stake is set midway between two points. The process is called:
questions.expl: This process is called double sighting.

questions.text: The permanent adjustment of theodolite includes:
questions.expl: Permanent adjustments include telescope and vertical circle index adjustments.

questions.text: The adjustment of horizontal cross hair is required particularly when the instrument is used for
questions.expl: The horizontal cross hair adjustment is essential when the instrument is used for levelling.

questions.text: A point of reference with a known elevation is
questions.expl: This is the definition of a benchmark.

questions.text: Which of the following branch of surveying is used to find the elevations of given points with respect to given or assumed datum?
questions.expl: Levelling is used to determine elevations relative to a datum.

questions.text: Reciprocal levelling in surveying eliminates which one of the following errors?
options: Errors due to earth's curvature, atmospheric correction and mistakes in recording staff readings
Errors due to earth's curvature, line of collimation and mistakes in recording staff readings
Errors due to atmospheric correction, line of collimation and mistake in recording staff readings
Errors due to earth's curvature, atmospheric correction and line of collimation
questions.expl: Reciprocal levelling eliminates errors due to curvature, refraction, and collimation.

questions.text: Consecutive readings with a dumpy level: 0.695, 1.525, 2.395, 0.635, 0.605, 0.805, 0.125. Instrument shifted after the third and fifth readings. The readings 2.395 and 0.635 represent
questions.expl: Reading before a shift is a foresight; reading after a shift is a backsight, so 2.395=FS and 0.635=BS.

questions.text: The height of instrument is equal to:
options: Reduced level of bench mark + back sight
Reduced level of bench mark + fore sight
Reduced level of bench mark + intermediate sight
questions.expl: HI = RL of BM + Back Sight.

questions.text: What is the main use of a "Surveyor's Level"?
options: To measure vertical distances and angles
questions.expl: A surveyor's level is primarily used to determine differences in elevation.

questions.text: In a survey, what is meant by the term "benchmark"?
options: A reference point used to measure elevation
A point used to measure distances
A reference point for horizontal angles
A standard unit for measuring lengths
questions.expl: A benchmark is a reference point of known elevation.

questions.text: In surveying, what is a "levelling" instrument used for?
questions.expl: A levelling instrument is used to determine vertical elevations.

questions.text: What is the use of a "dumpy level" in surveying?
questions.expl: A dumpy level is used to determine elevation differences between points.

questions.text: A vertical line which is perpendicular to the level line is called:
questions.expl: A plumb line is vertical and perpendicular to the level line.

questions.text: Which of the following methods of levelling yields inaccurate results?
questions.expl: Barometric levelling is the least accurate method as it depends on atmospheric pressure.

questions.text: In reciprocal leveling, the error which is not completely eliminated is due to:
options: Non adjustment of line of collimation
questions.expl: Refraction is not fully eliminated by reciprocal levelling since atmospheric refraction may vary between the two observation times.

questions.text: Which one of the following expressions is correct as per the height of instrument is concerned?
options: Sum of BS − Sum of FS = First RL − Last RL
Sum of FS − Sum of BS = Last RL − First RL
Sum of BS − Sum of FS = Last RL − First RL
Sum of FS − Sum of BS = First RL − Last RL
questions.expl: ΣBS − ΣFS = Last RL − First RL (rise of last station over first).

questions.text: The height of collimation is generally used in ___.
questions.expl: The height of collimation (HI) method is used in differential (ordinary) levelling.

questions.text: The elevation of plane of sight with respect to assumed datum is called:
questions.expl: This defines the Height of Instrument (HI).

questions.text: Which one of the formula is correct for estimation of RL of intermediate point?
questions.expl: RL of intermediate point = RL of BM + BS - IS (via Height of Instrument).

questions.text: Which type of levelling is used for establishing a benchmark with high precision at widely distant points?
questions.expl: Precise levelling is used for establishing high-precision benchmarks over long distances.

questions.text: The relationship between curvature correction Cc and refraction correction Cr for levelling works is given as:
questions.expl: Refraction correction is approximately 1/7th of the curvature correction.

questions.text: The curvature correction in leveling is always:
questions.expl: The curvature correction is always negative (subtractive) to the staff reading.

questions.text: Which of the following types of levelling cannot be done with a dumpy level?
questions.expl: Trigonometric levelling requires angle measurement and cannot be done with a dumpy level.

questions.text: Mean Sea Level (MSL) adopted by Survey of India for reference, is located at?
questions.expl: The Survey of India adopted MSL at Mumbai (Bombay) as the reference datum.

questions.text: Angles that can be set out with a French cross staff are
questions.expl: The French (octagonal) cross staff can set out 45° and 90° angles.

questions.text: A survey line joining subsidiary stations to the main line is called as
questions.expl: A tie line connects subsidiary stations to the main survey line.

questions.text: Chain surveying is most suitable when:
options: area to be surveyed is small
ground is fairly level and open with simple details
plans are required on a large scale
questions.expl: All these conditions favor the use of chain surveying.

questions.text: A tie line in a chain surveying:
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixes up the directions of all other lines
questions.expl: Tie lines are primarily used to locate details away from the main survey lines.

questions.text: In surveying, what is the 'chain' used for?
options: Checking the level of the ground
questions.expl: A chain is used to measure horizontal distances.

questions.text: Distance of an object from survey line is called:
questions.expl: This is the definition of an offset.

questions.text: The short offsets in chain survey are the ones whose length is ___.
questions.expl: Short offsets are generally those under 15m in length.

questions.text: The distance between two brass rings in a surveyor's chain is:
questions.expl: Each link in a metric chain is 0.2m (20cm), marked by rings at intervals.

questions.text: In which of the following branches of surveying the chain will not be used for measuring distances?
questions.expl: In tacheometric surveying, distances are found from stadia readings, not by chaining.

questions.text: The chain which is commonly used for measuring fields in cadastral survey is called:
questions.expl: The revenue chain is used for cadastral/revenue surveys.

questions.text: The errors such as sag in chain and chain not being horizontal during stepping are common in:
questions.expl: These errors are common during slope (stepping) measurement.

questions.text: The diameter of a link of a survey chain made up of galvanized mild steel wire is ___.
questions.expl: The wire diameter used for chain links is typically 4mm.

questions.text: The permissible limit of error in chaining for measurements over rough or somewhat hilly ground is 1 in ___.
questions.expl: The permissible error for rough/hilly ground chaining is about 1 in 500.

questions.text: Which one of the following triangles is most accurately plotted in chain surveying?
questions.expl: An equilateral (well-conditioned) triangle is plotted most accurately.

questions.text: The longest chain line used in making a survey is called
questions.expl: The longest chain line in a survey is called the baseline.

questions.text: The length of each link in an Engineer's chain is:
questions.expl: Each link of an Engineer's chain is 1.0 foot long.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most accurate and common method of measuring distance?
questions.expl: Chaining is the most common and accurate direct method of distance measurement in ordinary surveying.

questions.text: The angles of a well-proportioned triangle in a chain survey should not be:
questions.expl: Angles of a well-conditioned triangle should not exceed 120° (or be less than 30°).

questions.text: Which book is used for recording all observations and measurements taken during chain surveying?
questions.expl: The field book is used to record chain survey observations.

questions.text: Metric chains consists of ___ links.
questions.expl: A standard (20m) metric chain consists of 100 links.

questions.text: Which statement is true for chain surveying?
options: They are formed of straight links of Galvanized mild steel wires.
To facilitate easy reading of the chain, brass tallies are provided.
It is to be noted that length of a link is the distance between centres of two consecutive middle rings.
questions.expl: All the given statements describe features of chain surveying equipment.

questions.text: No angular measurements are made in surveying.
questions.expl: Chain surveying involves only linear measurements, no angular measurements.

questions.text: How many types of errors in chaining are available?
questions.expl: There are three types of errors in chaining (instrumental, personal, natural or cumulative/compensating/mistakes).

questions.text: In chain surveying, the area to be surveyed is divided into a number of small well conditioned triangles. Which condition should the triangle satisfy?
options: No angle is less than 50° or greater than 100°
An angle is less than 20° or greater than 130°
An angle is less than 30° or greater than 120°
No angle is less than 30° or greater than 120°
questions.expl: A well-conditioned triangle should have no angle less than 30° or greater than 120°.

questions.text: What is the term used in chain surveying, for the lateral distance measured perpendicular to the chain line?
questions.expl: This defines a perpendicular offset.

questions.text: Number of links in a 30 m metric chain is
questions.expl: A 30m metric chain has 150 links (each link 0.2m).

questions.text: Base line in the layout of a chain survey is:
questions.expl: The base line is the longest main survey line.

questions.text: The position of a point can be fixed more accurately by
questions.expl: Perpendicular offsets give the most accurate fixing of points in chain surveying.

questions.text: For a well-conditioned triangle, no angle should be less than
questions.expl: A well-conditioned triangle should have no angle less than 30°.

questions.text: Number of links in a 30 m metric chain is
questions.expl: A 30m metric chain has 150 links.

questions.text: When two points of surveying are mutually invisible the following method of ranging is adopted?
questions.expl: Indirect (reciprocal) ranging is used when the two points are mutually invisible.

questions.text: The total number of links provided in a Gunter's chain is?
questions.expl: A Gunter's chain has 100 links (66 feet total length).

questions.text: Survey line provided to verify the accuracy of the frame work is known as?
questions.expl: A check line is used to verify the accuracy of the survey framework.

questions.text: If the angle of intersection of a curve is θ, then the deflection angle will be
questions.expl: Deflection angle Δ = 180° - angle of intersection (θ).

questions.text: In setting out of curve by deflection angle, what is the general rule of deflection angle of a chord?
options: Deflection angle = deflection angle of the previous chord + tangential angle of the present chord
questions.expl: By Rankine's method, deflection angle = previous deflection angle + tangential angle of current chord.

questions.text: The radial offset at a distance X from the point of commencement of curve of radius R is given by
questions.expl: The radial offset formula is R - √(R²-X²).

questions.text: If the radius of a simple curve is R, then the length of the chord for calculating the offsets by the method of chords produced should not exceed
questions.expl: The chord length should not exceed R/20 for the method of chords produced.

questions.text: If the radius of a simple curve is R, then the length of the chord for calculating the offsets by the 'method of chords produced' should not exceed
questions.expl: The chord length should not exceed R/20 for the method of chords produced.

questions.text: The total angle of deflection of a transition curve is equal to:
questions.expl: The total deflection angle of a transition curve equals the spiral angle.

questions.text: If L is the length measured along the curve from the tangent point and R is the radius of curvature at the point as per the fundamental requirement of transition curve, the relation between these two is:
questions.expl: The fundamental requirement of a transition curve is that LR = constant.

questions.text: When the straight lines which the two curves connect are nearly parallel or intersect at a small angle, which type of curve is used?
questions.expl: A reverse curve is used when lines are nearly parallel or intersect at a small angle.

questions.text: The relation between the radius (R) and degree (D) of a curve is
questions.expl: The relation is R = 1719/D (for a 30m/100ft chord).

questions.text: What would be the sensitivity of a non-flexible module?
questions.expl: A non-flexible (rigid) module has zero sensitivity.

questions.text: A plan or map represents:
questions.expl: A plan/map is the projection of ground features on a horizontal plane.

questions.text: The primary objective of surveying is:
questions.expl: The primary objective of surveying is to prepare a plan or map.

questions.text: The basic principles of surveying needs to be followed for accurately locating the points on:
questions.expl: Surveying principles apply generally to locating points on the earth's surface.

questions.text: A ___ is established parallel to the sewer centre line at a distance that will not disturb and covered excavated material during setting out of Sewer Centre Line.
questions.expl: An offset line is set parallel to the sewer centre line to avoid disturbance from excavation.

questions.text: As Error increases, aspect ratio:
questions.expl: As error increases, the aspect ratio L/D generally decreases.

questions.text: Line joining equal rain fall readings on map is called ___.
questions.expl: Isohyetal (isohyet) lines connect points of equal rainfall.

questions.text: The relative positions of the points to be surveyed should be located by measurement from at least:
questions.expl: Points should be fixed using measurements from at least two points of reference.

questions.text: ___ is the act of making measurement of the relative position of natural and manmade features on earth's surface and the presentation of this information either graphically or numerically.
questions.expl: This is the definition of surveying.

questions.text: Which of the following is the principle of surveying working from whole to part?
options: The surveying is to work from part to part the area to fix the best positions of survey lines and survey stations.
The surveying is to work from around the complete area to fix the best positions of survey lines and survey stations
Principles of surveying working from part to whole only.
questions.expl: Working from whole to part means surveying the complete area first to fix the best positions of survey lines and stations.

questions.text: Three main phases of survey process are
options: Prepare the charts, planes and maps
Adopted survey method, successful planning and execution
Reconnaissance, field work and measurements and office work
questions.expl: The three main phases are reconnaissance, field work/measurements, and office work.

questions.text: The principle of "working from whole to part" is used in surveying because
options: Survey work can be completed quickly
questions.expl: This principle prevents accumulation and propagation of errors.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: a. Topographical survey b. Geodetic survey c. Engineering survey d. Cadastral survey with 1. Data for project 2. Boundaries of fields/buildings 3. Size and slope of earth 4. Natural features of the country
questions.expl: Correct matching: Topographical-natural features(4), Geodetic-earth size/slope(3), Engineering-project data(1), Cadastral-boundaries(2).

questions.text: Which of the following can be shown in a plan?
questions.expl: All of these features can be depicted on a plan.

questions.text: Which one of the following methods would give accurate results in determining the direction of observer's meridian?
options: Observation of circumpolar stars on the same vertical.
Observation of circumpolar stars at culmination.
Observation of the sun at the equal altitudes.
questions.expl: Observing circumpolar stars at culmination gives an accurate determination of the meridian.

questions.text: Statement (I): The fundamental principle of surveying is 'to work from the whole to the part'. Statement (II): Working from the whole to the part ensures prevention of accumulation of possible errors in survey work over large areas.
options: Both I and II are true, and II correctly explains I
Both I and II are true, but II does not explain I
I is true, II is false
I is false, II is true
questions.expl: Both statements are true, and statement II correctly explains the reasoning behind statement I.

questions.text: Consider the following statements with regard to Global Positioning Systems (GPS): 1. The position of an object can be exactly determined by a single satellite; 2. The position of the observer on ground is determined by an orbiting satellite; 3. Atomic clocks are fixed in satellites to calculate the positioning of the satellite to aid in determining travel times. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.expl: Statement 1 is false (a single satellite cannot fix a position); statements 2 and 3 correctly describe GPS operation.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding Remote Sensing Survey: 1. Information transfer is accomplished by use of electromagnetic radiation; 2. Remote Sensing from space is done by satellites; 3. Remote Sensing has no application in Earthquake prediction. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.expl: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is false since remote sensing does have earthquake-related applications.

questions.text: Number of satellites involved in the orbit for the GPS survey technique?
questions.expl: The GPS constellation consists of 24 satellites.

questions.text: Bowditch rule is applicable
options: where linear measurements are more precise than angular measurement
where linear and angular measurements are of equal precision
where angular measurements are more precise than linear measurement
In all cases of traverse adjustments
questions.expl: Bowditch's rule assumes linear and angular measurements are of equal precision.

questions.text: Which of the following traverse adjusting methods is employed for angular measurements?
questions.expl: The transit rule is used when angular measurements are more precise than linear ones.

questions.text: In the axis method of adjusting a traverse, the correction to any length is denoted as:
options: that length × (1/2 closing error/length of axis)
that length × (0.25 × closing error/length of axis)
that length × (0.75 × closing error/length of axis)
questions.expl: In the axis method, correction = length × (closing error/length of axis).

questions.text: If the whole circle bearing of a traverse line is between 270° to 360°, the signs of latitude and departure are:
questions.expl: In the NW quadrant (270°-360°), latitude is positive (north) and departure is negative (west).

questions.text: In which method of adjusting a traverse, the errors in linear measurements are proportional to √l? (Where l is the length of a line)
questions.expl: Bowditch's rule assumes errors are proportional to √l.

questions.text: If N is the number sides of the traverse, the sum of measured interior angles should be equal to:
questions.expl: Sum of interior angles of a closed traverse = (2N-4) × 90°.

questions.text: Which of the following are the total linear errors of closure in the compass traverse?
questions.expl: The typical permissible linear error of closure in compass traversing is about 1 in 5000.

questions.text: DMD states
questions.expl: DMD stands for Double Meridian Distance.

questions.text: Which method is used for making angular measurements when triangulation surveying is not possible?
questions.expl: Traverse surveying is used for angular measurements when triangulation isn't feasible.

questions.text: ___ is the sum of meridian distance of two ends of a line.
questions.expl: This is the definition of Double Meridian Distance (DMD).

questions.text: In a closed traverse, if algebraic sum of latitudes ΣL = negative and algebraic sum of departures ΣD = positive, the whole circle bearing of the error of closure will be between
questions.expl: Negative latitude (south) and positive departure (east) place the closing error bearing in the SE quadrant, WCB 90°-180°.

questions.text: In a cross traverse, the sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of departures exceeds the sum of west departures. The closing line will lie in the
questions.expl: Net south latitude and net east departure place the closing line in the SE quadrant.

questions.text: The sum of the interior angles of a closed traverse is equal to:
questions.expl: Sum of interior angles = (2n−4)×90°.

questions.text: The optical square is used to measure angles by:
questions.expl: The optical square works on the principle of double reflection.

questions.text: In this system, the shutter has the top and the bottom supports and rotates about a vertical axis passing through them.
questions.expl: This describes a pivot system rotating about a vertical axis.

questions.text: On a diagonal scale, it is possible to read up to
questions.expl: A diagonal scale can measure up to three dimensions (units, tenths, hundredths).

questions.text: Which of the following is not a basic component of a total station?
questions.expl: A total station is electronic and does not use a vernier scale.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a basic component of a total station?
questions.expl: A total station is electronic and does not use a vernier scale.

questions.text: On a diagonal scale, it is possible to read up to
questions.expl: A diagonal scale can measure up to three dimensions (units, tenths, hundredths).

questions.text: Which Cross Staff can be used to set up any angles (not just 90° and 45°)?
questions.expl: The adjustable cross staff can be set to any angle, unlike fixed types.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments is NOT used for measurement of angles?
questions.expl: A dumpy level is used for levelling (elevation), not angle measurement.

questions.text: Which size (diameter) of theodolite is generally preferred for general survey and engineering work?
questions.expl: Theodolites of 8 to 12 cm size are commonly used for general engineering survey work.

questions.text: The device used for measuring distances by attaching it to the wheel of a vehicle is called ___.
questions.expl: An odometer measures distance via a wheel attached to a vehicle.

questions.text: The tape which is commonly preferred for the works which need highest precision in measurement of base lines in triangulation is called ___ tape.
questions.expl: Invar tapes have a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, ideal for precise base line measurement.

questions.text: Which one of the following instruments is better and accurate in measurement of right angles?
questions.expl: The optical square (using double reflection) gives the most accurate right angles.

questions.text: The total station is the one which is the combination of:
questions.expl: A total station combines an electronic theodolite with an EDM.

questions.text: Which size (diameter) of theodolite is generally preferred for triangulation work?
questions.expl: Larger theodolites (14-25cm) are preferred for high-precision triangulation work.

questions.text: Which of the following classification in surveying is based on the surface and the area used?
questions.expl: Classification of this type is generally based on the instrument used, here theodolite surveys.

questions.text: An instrument used in surveying to compute the area of any given plane is known as;
questions.expl: A planimeter is used to compute plane areas.

questions.text: Which given telescope is used for precise work, gives accurate line of sight and can easily take inclined sights?
questions.expl: The telescopic alidade provides an accurate line of sight and can take inclined sights.

questions.text: Which of the following is a simplest and inexpensive instrument?
questions.expl: The non-transit theodolite is simpler and less expensive than transit types.

questions.text: The sensitivity of a bubble can be increased by:
options: increasing the diameter of the tube
increasing the radius of curvature of the tube
increasing the length of the tube
increasing the length of the divisions
questions.expl: Increasing the radius of curvature of the bubble tube increases its sensitivity.

questions.text: Two objects may be visualized simultaneously by a:
questions.expl: A sextant allows simultaneous viewing of two objects (for angle measurement).

questions.text: The cross hairs in the surveying telescope are placed
options: midway between eye piece and objective lens
much closer to the eye-piece than to the objective lens
much farther to the eye-piece than to objective lens
anywhere between eyepiece and objective lens
questions.expl: The cross hairs (diaphragm) are placed much closer to the eyepiece than to the objective lens.

questions.text: A metallic tape is made of
questions.expl: A metallic tape is made of cloth interwoven with wire.

questions.text: Size of a theodolite is specified by
questions.expl: Theodolite size is specified by the diameter of the lower (graduated) plate.

questions.text: In an internal focusing type of telescope, the lens provided is
questions.expl: An internal focusing telescope uses a concave (diverging) focusing lens.

questions.text: Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
questions.expl: Sensitivity of a level tube is designated by its radius of curvature.

questions.text: The multiplying constant of a theodolite is
questions.expl: The multiplying constant is given by f/i (focal length divided by stadia hair spacing).
